reuse.why: All consumers reuse the existing recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, although occurrence search policies remain scattered.

duplication.why: Holiday matching and date movement are centralized, but the new range handler repeats the enabled-adjustment dispatch used by other consumers.

placement.why: Calendar rules remain in shared schedules utilities, configuration metadata flows through rule parsing, and the endpoint lives alongside existing schedule handlers.

scope.why: The edits address the four requested schedule changes and their affected consumers without unrelated modifications.

maintainability.why: The core adjustment rule is shared, but holiday-dependent search bounds are independently encoded in three consumers, coupling callers to policy details.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed date-adjustment consumers call getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated adjustment dispatch is explicit rather than disguised through renaming or restructuring.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains frequency and holidays parameters plus a daily-frequency branch returning null; all changed callers continue using it.
